subject: Surge capacity pricing model & reserved commit options

Subject: Surge capacity pricing model & reserved commit options

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, I wanted to start the thread to capture the options for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) pricing and the add-on for surge / autoscale capacity. High level ask from your side was: predictable baseline for steady-state batch inference, with ability to surge during monthly marketing spikes without over-provisioning.

To make the discussion concrete, can you confirm the following workload points?
- Baseline throughput target: ~250k tokens/minute (p50) during business hours
- Peak surge windows: 3–4 hours/day, 6–8 days/month (marketing campaigns)
- Target latency SLO: 200–300ms for 95th percentile

If those numbers look right I’ll send a sizing + pricing matrix that covers: baseline reserved commit (12/24/36 month), GPU pool sizing options (H100 vs A100 profiles), and two models for burst capacity: prepaid burst credits vs on-demand surge billing (per vGPU-minute).

I’ll also include a recommended cooldown policy (how long surge can run before we throttle) and a pre-warm option to reduce cold-start retries.

Cheers,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks, that summary is accurate. A couple clarifying Qs before you size things:
- Our baseline workload is a mix of short chat-style requests (~8 tokens/response) and long-form generation for summaries (~120 tokens). Can you show cost sensitivity for average response lengths of 20 vs 80 tokens?
- For surge: we need guarantees that a marketing spike (estimated 3x baseline for up to 90 minutes) won't drop requests. What's the realistic max multiplier you support without SLA impact?
- Any blackout windows where burst isn't available (maintenance, region limits)?

Procurement (cc) will need a high-level pricing model to route internally — they prefer seeing a per-month committed price + clearly separated surge line items.

Appreciate it — Maya

maya@acme-analytics.com | +1 212-555-0987

Subject: Re: Surge capacity pricing model & reserved commit options

Maya —

Appreciate the specifics. Attached is a compact pricing table (surge_pricing_table.csv) and a short rationale. Key proposal highlights below:

1) Baseline reserved commit options (examples for your workload profile)
- 12-month commit: baseline 4 x H100-equivalent vGPUs (est throughput ~260k tokens/min typical mix). Monthly list: $125,000 / mo
- 24-month commit: same sizing, discounted list: $102,000 / mo
- 36-month commit: $96,000 / mo (deepest discount, suitable if you want price stability)

2) Burst / surge models (two choices)
- Prepaid burst credits: buy blocks of burst capacity (e.g., 10k vGPU-min blocks); credits drawn during spikes. Credit unit price is lower — good if you can predict campaign volumes. Example: 10k vGPU-min block = $22,500 (effective $2.25 / vGPU-min)
- On-demand surge billing: pay-as-you-go at time of surge. Default surge rate: $3.75 / vGPU-min. Caps and cooldowns applied to protect fleet: default cap 2.5x baseline sustained for up to 45 minutes; extended surges subject to throttling or manual escalation.

3) Cooldown and pre-warm policy
- Cooldown window: after a continuous surge >30 minutes, the system will start shedding non-critical requests to protect the baseline. We can extend the cooldown to 90 minutes for a nominal add-on (pre-warm reservations).
- Pre-warm: persistent warm standby GPUs to reduce cold-start penalty (one-time provisioning fee + small monthly pre-warm reservation).

4) SLAs & throughput guarantees
- Baseline SLA (for reserved commit): 99.5% availability and latency targets as agreed in the contract; burst availability is best-effort but we provide priority routing for committed accounts during constrained windows.

5) Discount and packaging note
- For a 12-month commit we typically apply a standard 10% discount off list. With a 12-month commit + upfront payment and a joint marketing reference, we can go to 18% (subject to sales/finance approval). Lauren, Stephanie — can we confirm approval banding?

I attached the CSV with line-item math and a short MAP proposal. Happy to hop on a call to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: surge_pricing_table.csv, MAP_proposal_v1.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Folks —

Reviewing Ben’s numbers. Quick internal notes for offer packaging to Acme:
- Baseline commit pricing: 24-month offer (12–18% discount band) is safe for standard approval. 12-month at 18% only if we secure a marketing/reference clause and partial upfront.
- Burst concession: we can lower on-demand surge to $3.25 / vGPU-min for this account for first 6 months if they commit to a minimum prepaid burst block purchase (5k vGPU-min). That reduces our revenue risk and encourages predictability.
- Cooldown extension: offer 90-minute extended cooldown as a $1,500 / month add-on (covers pre-warm reservation overhead).

Finance check: contract_draft.docx should reflect the prepaid burst minimum and an explicit cap on total monthly surge spend (suggest default cap = 150% of committed monthly spend unless customer opts out).

Ben — go ahead and share the revised line item and include the DocuSign link when Maya thumbs up.

- Lauren
